label: digit 1 input at original positions 0-2
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the digit 1 in one of the first three original-phase steps (t = 0, 1, 2). Precision 1.0 and recall ~0.98 on dev, and about 99.9% of activation mass is covered. Magnitude falls off with position: at t=0 it hits the max (~2.1), at t=1 it is ~0.8 of max, and at t=2 it is ~0.4 of max. The dev counts per position are about equal, while mass shares are 0.47 / 0.35 / 0.18. At t=3 it fires weakly on a small fraction of 1 inputs (772 steps, ~0.1% of mass). It never fires on any other token, at t >= 4, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase, including when 1 is fed back as an output.

issues: Minor: the misses (742 steps on test, 772 on dev) are all digit 1 at t=3. They are weak, mostly 0.00-0.06 of max, and carry about 0.05% of mass, so they are a fringe of the same concept and not a separate class. This matches the explanation.

The profile backs the factual claims. Copy-phase and delimiter mass is 0. Every token other than 1 has 0 activations. t>=4 has 0. The per-t active counts are about equal (16.6k / 16.4k / 16.5k) with mass shares 0.466 / 0.351 / 0.182. Test precision is 1.0 with 0 false positives, recall is 0.985 and mass recall is 0.9995.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
